lessons.title: BLUF Core
lessons.summary: Lead with your recommendation before context.

blocks.heading: Why BLUF works
blocks.text: Leaders need decision-ready information quickly; BLUF reduces processing time.

examples.before: I wanted to share a few things we learned over the last month...
examples.after: We should shift 20% of budget to retention because churn rose 8%, and I need approval today.
examples.note: Conclusion first, then evidence, then ask.

takeaways: State the decision in your first sentence.
Always end with a concrete ask.

links.title: HBR: How to Write an Email That People Will Actually Read (BLUF)
YouTube: Lead with the Bottom Line Up Front (BLUF)

lessons.practicePrompt: Deliver a 30-second status update using BLUF.

lessons.title: De-Hedging Core
lessons.summary: Replace uncertain qualifiers with accountable language.

blocks.heading: What hedging signals
blocks.text: Phrases like "I think" or "maybe" can read as uncertainty when clarity is required.

blocks.heading: How to de-hedge
blocks.text: Name the decision, the owner, and the timeline directly.

examples.before: I think we might want to consider delaying launch.
examples.after: We should delay launch by one week to fix checkout stability issues.

takeaways: Avoid stacking multiple qualifiers in one sentence.
Use active voice with clear ownership.
State constraints as facts, not guesses.

links.title: TED: Speak with conviction by avoiding hedges

lessons.practicePrompt: Rewrite three hedged statements from your last meeting.

lessons.title: Conviction Under Q&A
lessons.summary: Stay decisive during pushback without overclaiming.

blocks.heading: Acknowledge + answer
blocks.text: Briefly acknowledge the concern, then return to your recommendation.

examples.before: Maybe we're wrong, but hopefully this works.
examples.after: That risk is real, and our mitigation plan covers it. We should proceed with phased rollout.

takeaways: Do not abandon your recommendation under pressure.
Address risk with a mitigation plan.

lessons.practicePrompt: Answer a skeptical stakeholder question in 20 seconds.

lessons.title: Rule of Three
lessons.summary: Use parallel triads to improve clarity and memorability.

blocks.heading: Why three is sticky
blocks.text: Three points are easy to process, recall, and repeat.

blocks.heading: Parallel structure
blocks.text: Keep grammar and cadence similar across all three points.

examples.before: Our goals are improving quality, we need to move faster, and ownership is also important.
examples.after: Our priorities are quality, speed, and ownership.

takeaways: Use short, parallel phrasing across each point.
Avoid mixing abstract and concrete levels in one triad.

lessons.title: Problem-Solution-Benefit
lessons.summary: Frame proposals in a persuasive, executive-ready arc.

blocks.heading: Narrative arc
blocks.text: Define pain clearly, propose the fix, then quantify value.

examples.before: We built a new dashboard and it has many features.
examples.after: Reporting delays cost us weekly. This dashboard automates reporting, saving six analyst hours per week.

takeaways: Always tie your solution to business impact.
